Read-only. 10 agents over server/src/modules/reports, dashboard, commissions, client. Cite-by-file:line.

## A. SURFACE INVENTORY

### 1. pipeline-velocity  [report endpoint]
- shows: Open-pipeline aging/velocity: per-stage open deal count + value, avg/median days in stage, oldest deal per stage, aging buckets (0-7/8-30/31-60/60+), top 10 stuck deals (>30 days). KPIs: avgDealAgeDays, totalOpenValue, openDealCount, stuckDealCount.
- source: getPipelineVelocityReport -> buildDealFilterSql(filters,'created_at'); deals d JOIN pipeline_stage_config p; value = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d', aliasedDealBestEstimateWithForecastSql('d')) [forecast_revenue->bid_board_total_sales->bid_estimate->dd_estimate->awarded_amount, zeroed if on_hold]; age = NOW()-d.stage_entered_at; open = p.slug NOT IN TERMINAL_STAGE_SLUGS
- at: server/src/modules/reports/sales-tier1-service.ts:465-566 (filter 143-163; value chain shared/deal-value-sql.ts:120-130)
- period date col: d.created_at (deal creation) gates membership; stage age computed off d.stage_entered_at (current-state, NOT period-bounded)
- gating: rep-visible (no requireDirector; parseSalesReportRequest forces ownerIds=[req.user.id] for role 'rep')
- FLAGS: Uses FORECAST-FIRST value chain (forecast_revenue first) for OPEN pipeline value — differs from pipeline-summary/pipeline-by-rep/director-scorecard which use best-estimate chain WITHOUT forecast_revenue, so open-pipeline $ here can exceed those reports for the same deals. Period keys off created_at while displayed age uses live NOW()-stage_entered_at.

### 2. closed-won-revenue  [report endpoint]
- shows: Booked won revenue: KPIs totalBookedRevenue, wonDealCount, avgDealSize, winRate (won/(won+lost)). Monthly revenue, byOwner (+largest won deal), byOffice (+% of total), byWorkflowFamily (service vs standard), top 10 deals.
- source: getClosedWonRevenueReport -> buildDealFilterSql(filters,'won_at'); won = p.slug IN WON_STAGE_SLUGS, lost = p.slug IN LOST_STAGE_SLUGS; revenue = aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql('d') [awarded_amount-first chain: awarded_amount->bid_board_total_sales->bid_estimate->dd_estimate, zeroed if on_hold]
- at: server/src/modules/reports/sales-tier1-service.ts:568-686 (terminalOutcomeDateSql 133-141)
- period date col: Synthetic 'won_at' = terminalOutcomeDateSql(): LOST -> COALESCE(actual_close_date, stage_entered_at); WON/else -> COALESCE(contract_signed_at, actual_close_date, stage_entered_at, updated_at). Monthly bucket uses same outcomeDate; topDeals.wonAt uses a DIFFERENT COALESCE order (contract_signed_at::date, actual_close_date, stage_entered_at::date, updated_at::date).
- gating: rep-visible (no requireDirector; rep scoped to own ownerIds)
- FLAGS: Won-value uses AWARDED-FIRST chain whereas pipeline-velocity/forecast-accuracy open values use FORECAST-FIRST/best-estimate — inconsistent revenue basis. 'won_at' is a synthesized COALESCE date, NOT a real won_at; the platform deals KPI/board instead determines Won purely by canonical won-family stage_id membership (no date), so date-windowing here can include/exclude deals the platform board counts.

### 3. lead-conversion  [report endpoint]
- shows: Lead funnel: totalLeads, qualified, inDeals, won; leadToDealRate, dealToWonRate; funnel stages; bySource (leads/qualified/converted/won/revenue); 6-month monthly trend; top 5 revenue sources.
- source: getLeadConversionReport -> buildLeadFilterSql(filters); leads l LEFT JOIN deals d ON d.source_lead_id=l.id; qualified = l.converted_at IS NOT NULL OR l.qualification_completed_at IS NOT NULL OR l.status='converted'; won = p.slug IN WON_STAGE_SLUGS; revenue = aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql('d')
- at: server/src/modules/reports/sales-tier1-service.ts:688-780 (buildLeadFilterSql 165-178)
- period date col: l.created_at (lead creation) for ALL summary/source/revenue scoping; monthly trend buckets on DATE_TRUNC('month', l.created_at). Deal/win side is NOT date-filtered.
- gating: rep-visible (no requireDirector; rep scoped via ownerIds -> buildLeadOwnerIdentitySql on l.assigned_rep_id)
- FLAGS: Period is lead-created date; a lead created in-window whose deal won years later still counts as 'won', and a lead created out-of-window is excluded even if its deal won in-window — so 'won' here is NOT comparable to closed-won-revenue's won-date window. 'qualified' is a lead-status/date OR-predicate, divergent from any stage-based definition.

- shows: Director KPI scorecard: totalPipelineValue, openDealCount, forecastCommit, forecastBestCase, winRate; risks (dealsAtRisk + value via engine, stalledAccounts, overdueTasks, missedFollowUps); rep performance table; office comparison; top 5 at-risk deals.
- source: getDirectorScorecard (performance-tier2-service.ts); deals d JOIN users u JOIN offices o JOIN psc; open value = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d') (best-estimate); forecast_commit FILTER slug IN COMMIT_STAGE_SLUGS; forecast_best_case FILTER slug IN COMMIT+BEST_CASE; winRate from won_lost CTE; at-risk via getDealAtRiskResult engine
- at: server/src/modules/reports/performance-tier2-service.ts:361-560 (COMMIT_STAGE_SLUGS :18)

### 13. forecast-accuracy  [report endpoint]
- shows: Forecast accuracy: KPIs commit, bestCase, pipelineWeighted, wonActual; monthly commit/bestCase/pipelineWeighted/wonActual; accuracy.variancePercent ((wonActual-commit)/commit*100); top 25 pipeline-at-risk deals with expected_close_date.
- source: getForecastAccuracyReport (performance-tier2-service.ts); deals d JOIN users u JOIN offices o JOIN psc; forecastValue = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d', aliasedForecastFirstDealValueSql('d')) [forecast-first chain]; weightedValue = forecastValue * stage-slug ladder (0.10 opportunity / 0.25 estimating-family / 0.50 estimate_sent_to_client-family / 0.75 contract-family / ELSE win_probability/100 default 10); wonActual = aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql('d')
- at: server/src/modules/reports/performance-tier2-service.ts:819-902 (weighting ladder 829-835, esp :832)
- period date col: commit/bestCase/pipelineWeighted summary = current-state (dealScope, no date). wonActual (won_period CTE) = buildWonDateSql COALESCE(contract_signed_at, actual_close_date AT TZ UTC, updated_at) within from..to. Monthly join keys off COALESCE(d.expected_close_date, actual_close_date, contract_signed_date, updated_at::date) per month bucket.
- gating: requireDirector (routes.ts:509).
- FLAGS: TWO conflicting definitions of 'estimate sent to client' commit treatment co-exist: COMMIT_STAGE_SLUGS (:18) classifies estimate_sent_to_client AS COMMIT for the unweighted `commit` KPI, while the weightedValue ladder (:832) weights the SAME slug at only 0.50 — internally inconsistent. Monthly uses d.contract_signed_date whereas summary wonDate uses d.contract_signed_at — two different signed-date columns in one report. variancePercent compares current-state commit (no date) against period-bounded wonActual — mismatched time bases.

> SLICE NOTES: CANONICAL STAGE SETS (single source: shared/src/types/workflow.ts via shared/pipeline-terminal-stages.ts:7-12): WON_STAGE_SLUGS = ['won','sent_to_production','service_sent_to_production','service_scheduled','service_complete','closed_won']; LOST_STAGE_SLUGS = ['lost','deal_canceled','production_lost','service_lost','closed_lost']; TERMINAL_STAGE_SLUGS = canonical 'won'+'lost' unioned with both sets. All 13 reports import these same constants, so won/lost stage-SET membership is consistent across reports. The DIVERGENCE is in (a) date columns, (b) value chains, and (c) commit/forecast weighting — not the won/lost slug lists.
> 
> THREE VALUE CHAINS coexist (shared/deal-value-sql.ts): (1) best-estimate OPEN chain bid_board_total_sales->bid_estimate->dd_estimate->awarded_amount = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql default — pipeline-summary, pipeline-by-rep, director-scorecard pipeline/forecast, regional-ownership, weighted-forecast, rep-activity stalled value; (2) forecast-first chain forecast_revenue->...->awarded_amount = aliasedDealBestEstimateWithForecastSql / aliasedForecastFirstDealValueSql — pipeline-velocity (open value) and forecast-accuracy (forecastValue); (3) awarded-first WON chain awarded_amount->bid_board_total_sales->bid_estimate->dd_estimate = aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql — all 'won revenue' figures (closed-won-revenue, win-loss totalValue, lead-conversion revenue, rep-performance won value, forecast-accuracy wonActual). All zero out value when on_hold=true. Net effect: the SAME open deal yields a higher value in pipeline-velocity/forecast-accuracy (forecast_revenue counted first) than in pipeline-summary/pipeline-by-rep/director-scorecard (forecast_revenue ignored) — a real cross-report $ inconsistency for open pipeline.
> 
> 'CLOSED/WON' COMPUTATION DIVERGES BY DATE COLUMN (critical): closed-won-revenue uses synthetic terminalOutcomeDateSql = COALESCE(contract_signed_at, actual_close_date, stage_entered_at, updated_at) (sales-tier1:133-141); win-loss uses COALESCE(actual_close_date, lost_at, updated_at) (service.ts:753); director-scorecard & forecast-accuracy wonActual use buildWonDateSql = COALESCE(contract_signed_at, actual_close_date AT TZ UTC, updated_at) (perf-tier2:169-174); win-rate-trend & rep-performance use deal_stage_history.created_at (transition event time, which counts reopened/re-closed deals multiple times — a different POPULATION, not just a different date); lead-conversion's 'won' is keyed off lead.created_at window with no won-date bound at all. None matches the platform-canonical Won basis: the deals KPI/board (server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:2399-2498) determines Won purely by canonical won-family stage_id membership (no date column), so any of these date-windowed report 'Won' counts can diverge from the platform board for the same period.
> 
> 'ESTIMATE SENT TO CLIENT' is identified everywhere by STAGE SLUG (estimate_sent_to_client / service_estimate_sent_to_client), never by a date column. Its forecast treatment is internally inconsistent: COMMIT_STAGE_SLUGS (perf-tier2:18) lists estimate_sent_to_client as COMMIT (director-scorecard forecastCommit and forecast-accuracy `commit` KPI count 100% of its value), yet the weightedValue ladder (perf-tier2:832) weights the same slug at only 0.50, and legacy weighted-forecast (service.ts:668) ignores stage entirely using per-deal win_probability (default 50). So three forecast surfaces assign three different probabilities to an 'estimate sent to client' deal. ANCHOR confirmed at performance-tier2-service.ts:18 and :832.
> 
> ROLE-GATING SUMMARY: requireDirector = win-loss, pipeline-by-rep, rep-performance, regional-ownership, director-scorecard, forecast-accuracy. Rep-visible (rep auto-scoped to self via parseSalesReportRequest routes.ts:98-106): pipeline-velocity, closed-won-revenue, lead-conversion, pipeline-summary, weighted-forecast, win-rate-trend. requireAnyRole: rep-activity (rep auto-scoped via resolveRepActivityScope).
> 
> OFFICE-SCOPING DIVERGENCE: regional-ownership scopes office via deal_scoping_intake.office_id (dsi) and DROPS deals lacking a scoping-intake row; all other tier-2 reports scope via users.office_id (JOIN offices o, buildOfficeMatcher); tier-1 sales reports match users.office_id OR deals.office_code (buildDealFilterSql:157-159). regional-ownership is the outlier and can under-count.
> 
> OTHER TIME-BASIS SMELLS: pipeline-summary and weighted-forecast routes accept from/to but pipeline-summary IGNORES them (pure snapshot). Several reports mix period-bounded sections with current-state sections in one payload (rep-activity timeline vs stalled list; forecast-accuracy current-state commit vs period wonActual variance). forecast-accuracy references BOTH d.contract_signed_at (summary, perf-tier2:171) and d.contract_signed_date (monthly join, perf-tier2:871) — two distinct columns for the signed date inside one report.

Stage-active set keyed off COALESCE(bid_board_stage_slug, psc.slug) vs TERMINAL_STAGE_SLUGS — different stage-resolution than tier-4 (psc.slug only).

### 16. lost-by-reason  [report endpoint]
- shows: Lost deals grouped by lost_reason (label + count + total value) with per-reason competitor sub-breakdown.
- source: getLostDealsByReason in service.ts. deals d LEFT JOIN lost_deal_reasons ldr JOIN pipeline_stage_config psc. Lost set = psc.slug IN LOST_OUTCOME_STAGE_SLUGS (= LOST_STAGE_SLUGS = canonical 'lost' + aliases deal_canceled/production_lost/service_lost/closed_lost). Value = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql("d") (best-estimate). Competitor = COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(d.lost_competitor),''),'Not specified').
- at: server/src/modules/reports/service.ts:971-1034 (route routes.ts:300-311)

So a deal whose terminal-lost lives only in bid_board_stage_slug while psc.slug is non-lost would be counted active here but lost elsewhere. No office/owner scoping — only date. - at: server/src/modules/reports/service.ts:1758-1791 (route routes.ts:373-388)

> 
> WON/REVENUE COLUMN + STAGE-SET DIVERGENCES (the critical metric-consistency findings):
> 1) WON VALUE COLUMN CHAIN is not uniform. 'Won' value uses aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql = AWARDED-FIRST chain (awarded_amount, bid_board_total_sales, bid_estimate, dd_estimate; on_hold→0) in revenue-by-type, lead-source-roi, market-mix, executive-trends, customer-concentration lifetime, won-summary. Definition lives in shared/deal-value-sql.ts:104-106,146-148.
> 2) OPEN/PIPELINE VALUE CHAIN splits into two families: (a) FORECAST-FIRST (forecast_revenue prioritized) used by tier-3 workflow-bottlenecks/project-readiness/portfolio-load and tier-4 customer-concentration open + executive-trends pipeline; (b) BEST-ESTIMATE (no forecast_revenue) used by legacy stale-deals, dd-vs-pipeline, lost-by-reason, and workflow-overview/lead-source-roi active value. Same conceptual 'open pipeline value' computed off different column chains across reports.
> 3) WON/LOST STAGE-SET RESOLUTION splits: legacy service.ts current-state reports (stale-deals, workflow-overview, dd-vs-pipeline, lead-source-roi active gate) resolve terminal/active via COALESCE(d.bid_board_stage_slug, psc.slug) NOT IN TERMINAL_STAGE_SLUGS (nonTerminalDealStageSql, service.ts:275-280), whereas ALL won/lost OUTCOME counting (revenue-by-type, lost-by-reason, lead-source-roi won/lost, market-mix, executive-trends, customer-concentration, won-summary) and ALL tier-3 active gates use psc.slug ONLY (psc.is_terminal or psc.slug IN WON/LOST_STAGE_SLUGS). A deal whose terminal outcome is recorded only in bid_board_stage_slug (mirror) while psc.slug lags would be classified differently by the two families.
> 4) WON PERIOD DATE COLUMN is the largest divergence. revenue-by-type and won-summary bound won by d.actual_close_date (canonical close date). lead-source-roi bounds the ENTIRE query (incl. won counts/value) by d.created_at. market-mix KPI/mix/breakdown bound won by d.created_at, but its quarterly tab bounds by COALESCE(actual_close_date, lost_at, updated_at). executive-trends uses FOUR different date keys (created_at for KPI/quarterly; dsh.created_at stage-event for monthly won/lost + winRateTrend; COALESCE(actual_close_date,updated_at) and COALESCE(lost_at,updated_at) for fallbacks). So 'Won Revenue' / 'won deals' for the same date range will legitimately differ across revenue-by-type, lead-source-roi, market-mix, and executive-trends.
> 5) forecast-variance is the standout: it derives BOTH the won-deal population (INNER JOIN deal_forecast_milestones where milestone_key='closed_won') AND the won amount (cw.awarded_amount) from deal_forecast_milestones, bounded by cw.captured_at — it never reads pipeline_stage_config, WON_STAGE_SLUGS, actual_close_date, or the deal value chains. It is structurally guaranteed to scrape a different won dataset than every other report and is the most likely 'report reading a different dataset than the platform' finding.
> 
> ROLE-GATING INCONSISTENCY: lost-by-reason, opportunity-vs-pipeline/dd-vs-pipeline, stale-deals, follow-up-compliance, workflow-overview have NO requireRole/requireDirector gate (rep-visible), while the structurally similar director analytics (revenue-by-type, lead-source-roi, forecast-variance, data-mining, won-summary, workflow-bottlenecks, project-readiness, portfolio-load) are requireDirector. lost-by-reason and dd-vs-pipeline additionally apply NO rep self-scoping, so a 'rep' role hitting them sees org-wide aggregates. tier-4 market-mix/customer-concentration/executive-trends are requireAnyRole but force ownerIds=[self] for reps (parseTier4Filters routes.ts:132-146).
> 
> OFFICE-FILTER SEMANTICS DIVERGENCE: lead-source-roi and data-mining filter office via dsi.office_id (deal_scoping_intake office); forecast-variance via u.office_id (rep office); tier-3 via deals.office_code + offices join (buildOfficeMatcher); tier-4 via buildOfficeExistsMatcher (u.office_id OR d.office_code). Four different notions of 'which office a deal belongs to'.
> 
> DATE-FILTER NO-OP SURFACES: workflow-overview accepts from/to at the route but the service ignores them (only repId is read) — a real bug-shaped inconsistency, since the FilterBar implies the data is date-bounded. workflow-bottlenecks/project-readiness/portfolio-load intentionally ignore date filters (documented current-state). stale-deals and dd-vs-pipeline take no date filter at all. data-mining uses only 'to' (as as-of), 'from' is inert for staleness.

- FLAGS: DEFAULT win_probability of 50 is hard-coded when win_probability is NULL (line 685) — silent assumption that unset deals are 50% likely. Date range defaults to Jan-1-of-current-year .. today (defaultDateRange, service.ts:40-47), so a fresh load only shows YTD even though it is a forward forecast. - source: runReportBuilder(); FROM deals d LEFT JOIN pipeline_stage_config psc LEFT JOIN users u. WHERE always: d.is_active=true, COALESCE(is_test_data,false)=false, aliasedReportableDealFilterSql('d') (on_hold false), plus optional rep/stage/source/region/deal_type/from/to. total_value = SUM(aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d')); win_rate = won/(won+lost)*100 by psc.slug IN WON_STAGE_SLUGS / WON+LOST; cycle = AVG(actual_close_date - created_at::date).

This is Monday-Sunday weeks. If the platform's WTD requirement is Sunday-Saturday, every weekly bucket here is off (a Sunday's activity is grouped into the PRIOR ISO week, and week boundaries shift one day vs a Sun-Sat WTD). 'month' dimension = TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month',...),'YYYY-MM'). age_in_stage_bucket buckets CURRENT_DATE - stage_entered_at into 0-6/7-13/14-29/30-59/60+ days. Date field is user-selectable across created_at/updated_at/expected_close_date/actual_close_date/contract_signed_at/contract_signed_date (lines 82-89) — so the SAME week/month grouping can key off entirely different columns per request, with no enforced consistency. win_rate measure uses WON_STAGE_SLUGS/LOST_STAGE_SLUGS (same canonical set) but applies aliasedActiveDealCountFilterSql guard; total_value has NO active/won-stage guard so it sums value across ALL matched rows incl terminal. NO office_id scoping at all (buildFilters, lines 181-207) — every rep/office's deals are aggregated together; only a rep role is auto-scoped to self (effectiveReportRepId, lines 163-169). Endpoint is requireAnyRole (admin/director/rep) — a rep can run arbitrary cross-region/source pivots over their own deals.

### 42. Forecast Milestone capture (forecast-milestones-service.ts)  [commissions surface]
- shows: Not a read endpoint — the WRITE path that populates deal_forecast_milestones snapshots (initial/qualified/estimating/closed_won) consumed by Forecast Variance. Stores per-milestone forecast_amount, awarded/bid/dd estimates, expected_close_date, assigned_rep_id, stage, workflow_route, captured_at.
- source: insertForecastMilestone INSERT INTO deal_forecast_milestones (...) ON CONFLICT (deal_id, milestone_key). forecast_amount = deriveForecastAmount = awarded_amount ?? bid_estimate ?? dd_estimate (else 0). Milestone keying: qualified = stage slug in {dd, opportunity}; estimating = {estimating, estimate_in_progress, service_estimating, estimate_under_review, estimate_sent_to_client, bid_sent}; closed_won = WON_DEAL_STAGE_SLUGS entry from a non-won prior stage.
- at: server/src/modules/reports/forecast-milestones-service.ts:104-119 (deriveForecastAmount), 144-236 (insert), 274-335 (transition keys), 337-384 (backfill)
- FLAGS: deriveForecastAmount (line 104) value chain = awarded ?? bid ?? dd — OMITS bid_board_total_sales and the on_hold-zeroing that the deals-table reports apply via aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql. So a forecast snapshot's stored amount can differ from what Pipeline Summary / Weighted Forecast would show for the same deal at the same time, and Forecast Variance compares these snapshot amounts (not deals-table values). QUALIFIED milestone keys off slugs {dd, opportunity} (line 15-18) — 'dd' is treated as qualified here while in the deals reports DD stages are the is_active_pipeline=false bucket excluded by default, a semantic mismatch. Backfill rows are captured with captureSource='audit_backfill' and captured_at from audit/close timestamps, mixing live and reconstructed data in the same dataset Forecast Variance reads.

> SLICE NOTES: DATASET SPLIT (the audit-critical finding): The forecast/report surfaces draw from TWO different datasets. (1) Most aggregates (Pipeline Summary, Weighted Forecast, Pipeline by Rep, Won/Closed-Won Summary, Win/Loss, Report Builder, Custom Execute) read the live `deals` table joined to `pipeline_stage_config`. (2) Forecast Variance ALONE reads `deal_forecast_milestones` (snapshots written by forecast-milestones-service.ts). The two use different value formulas: deals-table reports use aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql / aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql (on_hold zeroed; chains include bid_board_total_sales), whereas milestone snapshots use deriveForecastAmount = awarded ?? bid ?? dd (no bid_board_total_sales, no on_hold zeroing). A report scraping milestones will not reconcile against the platform's deals-based KPIs.
> 
> WEEK / WTD (the explicitly requested finding): The Report Builder is the only surface with a week grouping. report-builder-service.ts:110 uses `TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('week', <dateField>), 'IYYY-IW')`. Postgres DATE_TRUNC('week',...) snaps to MONDAY, and 'IYYY-IW' is ISO-year/ISO-week. This is a Monday-start (Mon-Sun) week. Against a Sunday-Saturday WTD requirement it is wrong on both ends: Sundays fall into the prior ISO week, and every weekly bucket boundary is shifted by one day. There is NO Sunday-anchored or Sun-Sat week option anywhere. Period groupings the builder supports (dimension list, lines 16-24 / 95-122): stage, rep, region, source, deal_type, month (DATE_TRUNC('month') -> 'YYYY-MM'), week (DATE_TRUNC('week') -> 'IYYY-IW', ISO Monday), age_in_stage_bucket (CURRENT_DATE - stage_entered_at::date buckets: 0-6 / 7-13 / 14-29 / 30-59 / 60+ days). The builder's date field is user-selectable (created_at, updated_at, expected_close_date, actual_close_date, contract_signed_at, contract_signed_date; lines 82-89), so the same month/week grouping can key off any of six columns with no enforced consistency. Report Schedules cadence options are daily/weekly/biweekly/monthly/quarterly only — no WTD/weekday anchoring.
> 
> PERIOD DATE-COLUMN INCONSISTENCY across the won/forecast family: Weighted Forecast keys on expected_close_date; Won/Closed-Won Summary keys on actual_close_date ONLY; Win/Loss keys on COALESCE(actual_close_date, lost_at, updated_at); Forecast Variance keys on deal_forecast_milestones.captured_at. So 'won deals in May' can yield four different deal sets depending on which surface you ask. getPipelineSummary even accepts from/to params (routes.ts:192-193) that are silently ignored by its SQL.
> 
> ROLE-GATING SUMMARY: requireDirector — win-loss, activity-summary, revenue-by-type, lead-source-roi, forecast-variance, data-mining, won-summary, closed-won-summary, pipeline-by-rep, rep-performance, regional-ownership, director-scorecard, forecast-accuracy, workflow-bottlenecks, project-readiness, portfolio-load, POST /execute. rep-visible (no gate, reps auto-scoped to self) — pipeline-summary, weighted-forecast, win-rate-trend, workflow-overview, stale-deals, lost-by-reason, follow-up-compliance, opportunity-vs-pipeline. requireAnyRole (admin/director/rep) — POST /run (report builder), rep-activity, market-mix, customer-concentration, executive-trends. NO role gate at all (only auth + visibility WHERE) — every /saved*, /schedules, /runs CRUD route. NO office_id scoping exists in any of the deals-table aggregate functions inspected (getPipelineSummary, getWeightedPipelineForecast, getPipelineByRep, getClosedWonSummary, getWinLossRatioByRep, runReportBuilder, executeCustomReport) — only Forecast Variance / regional-ownership / lead-source-roi apply an office filter (and Forecast Variance filters on the REP's u.office_id, not the deal's office). A director or rep in one office therefore sees cross-office data in the core pipeline/won reports.
> 
> WON/LOST SLUG SETS (shared/src/types/workflow.ts:309-315, 289-302): WON_DEAL_STAGE_SLUGS = canonical 'won' (outcomeCategory='won') + aliases {sent_to_production, service_sent_to_production, service_scheduled, service_complete, closed_won}. LOST_DEAL_STAGE_SLUGS = canonical 'lost' + aliases {deal_canceled, production_lost, service_lost, closed_lost}. TERMINAL_STAGE_SLUGS (server/src/modules/shared/pipeline-terminal-stages.ts:7-9) = union of canonical terminal + won + lost. nonTerminalDealStageSql (service.ts:275-280) uses COALESCE(d.bid_board_stage_slug, psc.slug) NOT IN TERMINAL_STAGE_SLUGS, but getPipelineSummary at service.ts:627 uses COALESCE(d.bid_board_stage_slug,'') — divergent terminal-exclusion logic between the shared helper and Pipeline Summary.
> 
> POTENTIAL SECURITY/CONSISTENCY SMELLS worth flagging to the audit: (a) PATCH /saved/:id can set visibility='company' without the admin check that POST /saved enforces (routes.ts:771 vs 791) — privilege drift. (b) executeCustomReport injects is_active/test-data/on_hold guards ONLY for entity='deals' (service.ts:2592-2596); contacts/activities/tasks exports include inactive/test rows. (c) Report run/schedule executor is not present in this module — createReportRun only writes status='queued'; resultUri/runtimeMs never populated here, so 'scheduled reports' are currently non-functional stubs as far as these files show.

> SLICE NOTES: CANONICAL Won = the director 'Closed {period}' KPI card, fed by getWonCloseSummary (server/src/modules/dashboard/service.ts:2238-2271) on the deals.won_closed_date basis: WHERE COALESCE(is_test_data,false)=false AND COALESCE(on_hold,false)=false AND psc.slug IN WON_STAGE_SLUGS AND won_closed_date IS NOT NULL AND won_closed_date BETWEEN from/to [+scope]; value = SUM(aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql = COALESCE(awarded_amount, bid_board_total_sales, bid_estimate, dd_estimate where >0, 0), on_hold->0). aliasedWonHsClosedWonDateSql was FLIPPED to read the app-owned `d.won_closed_date` column (server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:970-981; previously hubspot_extra_properties->>'hs_closed_won_date'). This protects the 191 / $9,778,045.90 figure. The per-rep Closed column (getCanonicalRepWonSummary, service.ts:2287-2314) is byte-identical WHERE + GROUP BY, so it reconciles to the card BY CONSTRUCTION, with an 'Unassigned' remainder row forcing table+CSV == card.
> 
> KEY AUDIT FINDING — the dashboard module ITSELF contains FIVE distinct Won/win bases that reports must be checked against, because surfaces on the SAME director page disagree:
> 1. won_closed_date (CANONICAL): Closed KPI, forecast 'Closed', per-rep Closed column, CSV export.
> 2. deal_stage_history.created_at (stage-transition timing): getWinRateTrend (rep-detail trend chart) AND buildRepPerformanceCards rep_wins (leaderboard Win-rate FALLBACK). A rep's canonical 'N won' and their win-rate numerator are computed off different dates in the same table row.
> 3. COALESCE(actual_close_date, lost_at, updated_at): getWinLossRatioByRep -> rep DRILL-DOWN 'Win Rate · period' StatCard (director-rep-detail.tsx:545-550). This is the exact updated_at-fallback expression getWonCloseSummary's comment (service.ts:2243-2245) says 'inflated the card'. Drilling into a rep shows win/loss on a known-inflating basis that won't match the leaderboard 'N won'.
> 4. COALESCE(actual_close_date, contract_signed_date, contract_signed_at, lost_at, updated_at): getRecentCloses -> Recent Closes feed + 'Closing' tile won-count. Same inflating basis AND the ONLY Won-ish surface that OMITS COALESCE(is_test_data,false)=false — test deals can leak in and disagree with scopeSummary.won.count.
> 5. rep_performance_snapshots (worker-precomputed): Activity Pulse, Strategic Alerts, AI Coaching, leaderboard win-rate PRIMARY, sparkline/region. Deliberately retired for the Closed column (Wave-1 Finding D, stale/inflated) but still drives win-rate/activity/coaching, so those cells can contradict the live canonical Won.
> 
> Also (consistency surface area for the audit): (a) Period derivation differs by dashboard — director presetToDateRange (use-director-dashboard.ts:278-318) builds from/to from now.toISOString() (UTC), while the rep dashboard anchors 'today' to America/Chicago (service.ts:1349); a report keying Won by UTC vs CT can drift a day at midnight. (b) Active-pipeline and At-risk KPIs ignore the selected period (current-state) unlike the Closed card — same band, two temporal models. (c) The revenue GOAL behind pace/percent is HARD-CODED (@/lib/revenue-goal, goalSource:'none'). (d) Reps have NO Won/Closed card (routes.ts:22 /rep returns active deals/leads/commission only); canonical Won is director-gated (requireRole admin,director); 'team' scope short-circuits to data:null (routes.ts:63-67). (e) getWinLossRatioByRep INNER JOINs users (drops unassigned-rep wins) whereas getWonCloseSummary/getCanonicalRepWonSummary retain null-rep rows (surfaced via the Unassigned reconcile row) — another reason drill-down totals can undershoot the card. (f) WON_STAGE_SLUGS / WON_OUTCOME_STAGE_SLUGS / LOST_* lists come from server/src/modules/shared/pipeline-terminal-stages.js and reports module respectively — a report using a different stage-slug list than WON_STAGE_SLUGS would silently diverge from the canonical card.

> SLICE NOTES: SCOPE OF DATA SETS / DIVERGENT SOURCES (core of this audit):
> 
> 1. deal_payment_events (the collections ledger) -- reporting-service.ts is the ONLY application reader anywhere in the repo (verified: grep -rln 'deal_payment_events|dealPaymentEvents' returns only server/src/modules/commissions/reporting-service.ts, shared/src/schema/index.ts, shared/src/schema/tenant/deal-payment-events.ts). It is read in exactly three places, all in reporting-service.ts:
>    - getCommissionEarned per-deal paid_ytd: LEFT JOIN deal_payment_events pe ON pe.deal_id=d.id, SUM(CASE WHEN pe.paid_at::date >= utcBounds.yearStart THEN (is_credit_memo ? -ABS : ABS)(pe.gross_revenue_amount::numeric) ELSE 0 END) (lines 547-558).
>    - getCommissionSummary paid CTE: FROM deal_payment_events pe JOIN deals d JOIN pipeline_stage_config psc WHERE pe.paid_at::date >= utcBounds.yearStart, SUM(CASE WHEN pe.is_credit_memo THEN -ABS(pe.gross_revenue_amount::numeric) ELSE ABS(...) END) (lines 640-652).
>    Columns used: paid_at (timestamptz, .::date), gross_revenue_amount (numeric(14,2)), is_credit_memo (boolean) -- schema at shared/src/schema/tenant/deal-payment-events.ts:19-22. gross_margin_amount, recorded_by_user_id, notes are NEVER read by any reporting code.
> 
> 2. The dashboard module exposes a field literally named last_paid_at (server/src/modules/dashboard/service.ts:1084,1111) but it is COALESCE(d.contract_signed_at::date, d.contract_signed_date, dsc.contract_signed_date_at_signing) -- a contract-signed date, NOT a collections/ledger value (dashboardEarnedSignedDateSql, lines 986-988). Naming landmine: the dashboard's last_paid_at is unrelated to deal_payment_events.
> 
> 3. TWO INDEPENDENT COMMISSIONS AGGREGATIONS. Rep-facing /commissions -> getRepCommissionDashboard (reporting-service.ts) and director-facing 'Team Commissions' /director/commissions -> GET /dashboard/director/commissions (dashboard module) compute earned/potential through entirely separate queries and CAN disagree. Reps and directors are not guaranteed to see the same commission numbers.
> 
> 4. paid_ytd is always hardcoded to the UTC calendar year (currentUtcSummaryBounds.yearStart) in BOTH ledger reads -- it ignores filters.from/to. Earned in the same endpoints DOES honor filters.from/to (dateSql). A report for a historical window mixes period-correct earned with current-calendar-YTD paid.
> 
> 5. REP-ATTRIBUTION INCONSISTENCY FOR COLLECTIONS. getCommissionSummary's paid CTE scopes by d.assigned_rep_id (repSql, line 651 -- current owner) while earned scopes by dsc.rep_user_id (rep at signing, commissionRepSql). For a reassigned deal these point to different reps, so a rep's earned and paid can attribute to different people.
> 
> 6. DATE-COLUMN PROLIFERATION across surfaces -- each keys its period off a different column / COALESCE chain: commissions earned = COALESCE(contract_signed_at, contract_signed_date, dsc.contract_signed_date_at_signing); closed-won 'won_at' = CASE/COALESCE(contract_signed_at, actual_close_date, stage_entered_at, updated_at); director-scorecard = COALESCE(contract_signed_at, actual_close_date, updated_at); customer-concentration = COALESCE(actual_close_date, lost_at, updated_at); executive-trends closed = COALESCE(actual_close_date, updated_at); pipeline-velocity/market-mix = created_at; lead-conversion = leads.created_at; forecast-accuracy = expected_close_date; operations tier (workflow/project-readiness/portfolio) = current-state stage_entered_at (date range inert). A 'won' deal can fall in different months depending on which report you read.
> 
> 7. SOURCE-VALUE ORDER MISMATCH within commissions: earned/calculate path (service.ts resolveSourceValue, lines 36-49) uses awarded_amount -> bid_estimate -> dd_estimate; potential/pipeline path (aliasedDealBestEstimateSql) uses bid_board_total_sales -> bid_estimate -> dd_estimate with awarded_amount only as fallback (documented reporting-service.ts:202-204). A deal's projected (pipeline) commission and eventual earned commission are computed off different amounts even before any value change.
> 
> 8. ROLE-GATING SUMMARY. Server /commissions routes have NO role middleware (requireCrmUser only, app.ts:259) -- rep self-scoping enforced in code via effectiveRepForRepDashboard/effectiveCommissionRepId (role==='rep' forces userId). Client gates /commissions to ['rep'], /director/commissions to ['admin','director']. Reports routes: pipeline-velocity / closed-won-revenue / lead-conversion / market-mix / customer-concentration / executive-trends = requireAnyRole (rep-reachable, client-ungated); rep-activity = requireAnyRole + client ['admin','director','rep']; director-scorecard / forecast-accuracy / workflow-bottlenecks / project-readiness / portfolio-load = requireDirector + client ['admin','director']. All report endpoints are office-scoped via req.officeSlug ?? req.user.activeOfficeId ?? req.user.officeId; the commissions endpoints are NOT office-scoped (rep-scoped only).
> 
> 9. The Reports landing page (reports-page.tsx) is fully static and client-ungated (App.tsx:235): it advertises director-only reports to reps as 'Open' links blocked by RequireRole on navigation. The exported helper canViewDataMiningSection(role)==='director' is defined but unused there.
> 
> 10. getRepCommissionDashboard has a WRITE side-effect on a GET: refreshCommissionSnapshots UPSERTs commission_deal_snapshots on every dashboard load (reporting-service.ts:427), powering the per-deal 'delta since last update' -- so the delta is computed against the previous page load, not against any business event.

### SENT TO CLIENT (amount sent)
- CANONICAL: STAGE-based, not the proposalSentAt timestamp. Rep-facing canonical = the pipeline/deals-workspace 'Estimate Sent' column: value via dealPipelineValueSql('current')=dealBestEstimateSql(deals); membership = deal currently in an estimate-sent stage; the 'sent date' window resolves via dealEstimateSentAtSql() (MAX deal_stage_history.created_at of entry into estimate_sent stages, else stage_entered_at if currently in one). ESTIMATE_SENT_STAGE_SLUGS = ['estimate_sent_to_client','service_estimate_sent_to_client','bid_sent'].  @ server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:401 ESTIMATE_SENT_STAGE_SLUGS; :1018 dealEstimateSentAtSql (and :1077 workspaceEstimateSentAtSql for raw-SQL path); rep filter consumer client/src/pages/deals/deal-list-page.tsx:949 (estimateSentFrom/To) -> routes.ts:577; pipeline column value server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:2552 (dealPipelineValueSql) + :2539 addEstimateSentDateConditions
- COMPUTE: Membership: deal.stage_id resolves to slug IN ('estimate_sent_to_client','service_estimate_sent_to_client','bid_sent'). Amount per deal (pipeline 'current' value): COALESCE( CASE WHEN bid_board_total_sales>0 THEN bid_board_total_sales END, CASE WHEN bid_estimate>0 THEN bid_estimate END, CASE WHEN dd_estimate>0 THEN dd_estimate END, awarded_amount>0..., 0) with on_hold -> 0 (dealBestEstimateSql/aliasedDealBestEstimateSql). Sent-date window: dealEstimateSentAtSql() = COALESCE( (SELECT MAX(dsh.created_at) FROM deal_stage_history dsh JOIN pipeline_stage_config s ON s.id=dsh.to_stage_id WHERE dsh.deal_id=d.id AND s.slug IN (ESTIMATE_SENT_STAGE_SLUGS)), CASE WHEN current_stage.slug IN (ESTIMATE_SENT_STAGE_SLUGS) THEN d.stage_entered_at END ). NOTE: pipeline column value is point-in-time current-stage value, not an as-sent snapshot.
- DATE COL: Derived dealEstimateSentAtSql() (MAX deal_stage_history.created_at into an estimate-sent stage; fallback deals.stage_entered_at while currently in the stage). There is NO dedicated estimate_sent_at scalar column. Distinct from deals.proposal_sent_at (the proposal-card timestamp).
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: PARTIAL. A Sun-Sat WTD 'amount sent this week' would key off dealEstimateSentAtSql() (deal_stage_history entry into an estimate-sent stage) BETWEEN Sunday and Saturday, summing dealBestEstimateSql. Feasible per-department by joining office scope, but requires the stage-history subquery (heavier) and the amount is current-value not as-sent-value. proposal_sent_at would be simpler but is NOT the canonical/rep-visible basis.
- PER-REP: YES using the SAME source reps see: deals workspace already filters by estimateSentFrom/To via dealEstimateSentAtSql and shows the Estimate Sent column value (deals/service.ts:2539-2552). Slice by assigned_rep_id on the same query.

Estimating membership (when scoped): psc.slug IN ('estimating','service_estimating','estimate_under_review','estimate_in_progress','service_estimate_under_review') per CANONICAL_DEAL_WORKFLOW_CONTRACTS (shared/src/types/workflow.ts:101-122).
- DATE COL: NONE canonical. 'Estimated' is a current-state pipeline value (current stage membership), not a dated event. No estimate_created_at / estimating_entered_at column drives it. Period reports that need a date borrow created_at / expected_close_date / stage_entered_at depending on caller, which is itself a divergence vector.
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: WEAK as a flow metric: ESTIMATED has no event date, so a Sun-Sat 'amount estimated this week' has no canonical date column. The closest dated proxy is deal_stage_history entry into an estimating stage (parallel to the estimate-sent helper) but no helper exists today. A point-in-time 'open estimating value' per department/week (snapshot of dealBestEstimateSql for deals currently in estimating stages, office-scoped) is feasible.
- PER-REP: YES point-in-time: reps already see their Estimating column value (dealBestEstimateSql, deals/service.ts:2552) sliced by assigned_rep_id. A dated weekly flow per rep would need a new stage-history-entry helper.
  - DIVERGES @ Won deal value (awarded-first vs estimate-first) (server/src/modules/shared/deal-value-sql.ts:104 effectiveWonDealValueSql / :116 aliasedDealAwardedFirstWithFallbackSql vs :77 dealBestEstimateSql): Won metric reorders the SAME four columns to awarded_amount FIRST (AWARDED_FIRST_VALUE_CHAIN :32), whereas ESTIMATED puts bid_board_total_sales/bid_estimate first and awarded_amount last. Same columns, different precedence -> a deal's 'estimated' value can differ from its 'won' value.

So forecast/readiness reports value an estimating-stage deal by forecast_revenue first, diverging from the pipeline 'Estimating' column which uses best-estimate (no forecast_revenue).
  - DIVERGES @ Commission potential / pipeline value (adds change orders) (server/src/modules/commissions/reporting-service.ts:372,473,624 (aliasedDealBestEstimateSql + COALESCE(d.change_order_total,0))): Uses the same best-estimate chain BUT adds change_order_total, and restricts to commission 'potential' stage set (potentialStageSql :164). Pipeline 'Estimating' column does not add change orders.

Won) and lets the user choose any date field -- so an 'estimated value by month' report buckets by created_at/actual_close_date etc., none of which is an estimating event date.
  - DIVERGES @ AI copilot deal context (per-deal raw columns) (server/src/modules/ai-copilot/context-service.ts:75-76,169-171 (selects dd_estimate, bid_estimate, awarded_amount)): Reads the raw bid_estimate/dd_estimate/awarded_amount for a SINGLE deal's narrative context with no COALESCE precedence, no on_hold zeroing, no aggregation -- not a metric, but a divergent surfacing of the same underlying columns.

### COLLECTED (amount collected)
- CANONICAL: deal_payment_events ONLY. Sum of net cash: SUM(CASE WHEN pe.is_credit_memo THEN -ABS(pe.gross_revenue_amount) ELSE ABS(pe.gross_revenue_amount) END) keyed off pe.paid_at. The single consumer is commissions (the 'Paid YTD' figure). NOTE: the shared schema export obfuscates the table/column name to 'ln' (deal-payment-events.ts exports table 'ln' with numeric column 'ln') but it is physically deal_payment_events.gross_revenue_amount.  @ shared/src/schema/tenant/deal-payment-events.ts:13 table (paidAt:19, grossRevenueAmount:20, isCreditMemo:22); consumer server/src/modules/commissions/reporting-service.ts:640-652 (getCommissionSummary 'paid' CTE), also :547-553 paid_ytd per-deal
- COMPUTE: getCommissionSummary paid CTE: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN pe.is_credit_memo THEN -ABS(pe.gross_revenue_amount::numeric) ELSE ABS(pe.gross_revenue_amount::numeric) END),0)::numeric AS paid_ytd FROM deal_payment_events pe JOIN deals d ON d.id=pe.deal_id JOIN pipeline_stage_config psc ON psc.id=d.stage_id WHERE pe.paid_at::date >= yearStart AND COALESCE(d.is_test_data,false)=false AND COALESCE(d.on_hold,false)=false (notOnHoldDealSql) [+ repSql d.assigned_rep_id, + stageSql]. Credit memos subtract; positive payments add. Per-deal paidYtd (:547) is the same expression FILTERed to pe.paid_at::date >= yearStart.
- DATE COL: deal_payment_events.paid_at (cast ::date). YTD window = currentUtcSummaryBounds().yearStart (Jan 1 UTC). No MTD/period parameterization for collected -- it is hardcoded YTD in getCommissionSummary; the per-deal version is also YTD-anchored.
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: YES and cleanest of the four: per-department Sun-Sat WTD = SUM(net-of-credit-memo gross_revenue_amount) WHERE pe.paid_at::date BETWEEN Sunday AND Saturday, joined deals->office for department scope, excluding test/on-hold. paid_at is a real timestamp with btree indexes (deal_payment_events_paid_at_idx), so windowing is exact and fast. Only change vs today: parameterize the window instead of hardcoded yearStart.
- PER-REP: YES: the same query already supports repSql (d.assigned_rep_id) scoping; per-deal paidYtd is already shown to reps in the commissions earned table. Caveat: attribution is by deal.assigned_rep_id at query time, not by who was assigned when paid.
  - DIVERGES @ Per-deal Paid YTD column in commissions earned-deals table (server/src/modules/commissions/reporting-service.ts:547-553 (getCommissionEarned dealsResult)): Same net-of-credit-memo expression and same paid_at>=yearStart gate, but LEFT JOIN deal_payment_events per deal and aggregated per deal (GROUP BY deal). It additionally lives behind the signedDealSql()/notLostStageSql() commission filters, so it only surfaces collected $ for signed, non-lost, non-on-hold deals -- a narrower population than the summary 'paid' CTE which only excludes test/on-hold (not unsigned/lost). Two 'collected' numbers on the same page can differ by population.

### CLOSED (what a rep has closed = Won, booked)
- CANONICAL: deals.won_closed_date + Won-stage membership + awarded-first value. Helper aliasedWonHsClosedWonDateSql() returns `<alias>.won_closed_date`; dashboard getWonCloseSummary is the authoritative card and getCanonicalRepWonSummary is its exact per-rep decomposition (server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:970-980 + server/src/modules/dashboard/service.ts:2238-2314).  @ server/src/modules/dashboard/service.ts:2238 (getWonCloseSummary) and :2287 (getCanonicalRepWonSummary, per-rep); date helper server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:970-980
- COMPUTE: WHERE COALESCE(d.is_test_data,false)=false AND reportableDealSqlPredicate('d') [= COALESCE(d.on_hold,false)=false] AND psc.slug IN (WON_STAGE_SLUGS = 'won' + genuine won aliases) AND aliasedHasUsableWonDateSql('d') [d.won_closed_date IS NOT NULL] AND d.won_closed_date >= from::date AND d.won_closed_date <= to::date; value = COALESCE(SUM(aliasedEffectiveWonDealValueSql('d')),0) where that = CASE WHEN on_hold THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(awarded_amount>0, bid_board_total_sales>0, bid_estimate>0, dd_estimate>0, 0) END (deal-value-sql.ts:146-148 / 116-118 / 32-37). Per-rep version adds `d.assigned_rep_id AS rep_id` + GROUP BY only (byte-identical WHERE per the code comment at dashboard/service.ts:2280-2286). 'Closed' means Won ONLY -- lost is never folded into the per-rep closed value.
- DATE COL: deals.won_closed_date (app-owned, set by changeDealStage on Won entry, cleared on reopen/Lost; migration 0141). NOT actual_close_date (reseed-contaminated, explicitly forbidden -- deals/service.ts:955-966) and NOT contract_signed_at (reserved for commissions).
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: YES. Per-department: join deals->users->offices (or d.office_code) and group; per Sun-Sat WTD window, filter d.won_closed_date >= weekStart AND <= weekEnd with the same Won-stage + usable-date + on-hold + test-data predicates. won_closed_date is a plain date column so a [weekStart, weekEnd] BETWEEN is trivial. Do NOT use actual_close_date/updated_at for the window.
- PER-REP: YES, with exact platform parity. getCanonicalRepWonSummary (dashboard/service.ts:2287) IS the per-rep slice and is byte-identical to the card WHERE. The deals workspace Won column (getDealsForPipeline) and the /deals?won_since=&won_until= drill-down both gate on aliasedWonHsClosedWonDateSql=won_closed_date (deals/service.ts:906-908, 2505-2520), so a rep filtering their own won deals sees the same set. Use this source for any per-rep closed report.

Uses WON_OUTCOME_STAGE_SLUGS (=WON_STAGE_SLUGS) but NO won_closed_date guard and NO is_active handling parity. Per-rep totalValue here != getCanonicalRepWonSummary.closedValue.

### PROJECTED / EXPECTED-CLOSE (going-to-close 30/60/90)
- CANONICAL: There is NO single platform-blessed 30/60/90 projection. The closest report-canonical input is deals.expected_close_date as the projection date, combined with a deal value. Two coexisting computation families exist: (a) win_probability-weighted on expected_close_date month (getWeightedPipelineForecast), and (b) stage-weighted fixed-percentage on expected_close_date window (getForecastAccuracyReport). The schema forecast_* columns (forecast_window/category/confidence_percent/revenue/gross_profit on deals.ts:99-111) exist but are used ONLY as a value-COALESCE input (aliasedForecastFirstDealValueSql prefers forecast_revenue), never as the projection-date or confidence driver in any 30/60/90 query.  @ Projection-date column: deals.ts:169 (expected_close_date). win-prob weighted: server/src/modules/reports/service.ts:668-707. stage-weighted: server/src/modules/reports/performance-tier2-service.ts:829-835 (weights) + :880-894 (at-risk list gated on expected_close_date window).
- COMPUTE: (a) getWeightedPipelineForecast (reports/service.ts:678-698): GROUP BY TO_CHAR(d.expected_close_date,'YYYY-MM'); weighted_value = SUM(aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d') * COALESCE(d.win_probability,50)/100.0); WHERE d.is_active AND not test AND nonTerminalDealStageSql() AND d.expected_close_date BETWEEN from AND to. (b) getForecastAccuracyReport (performance-tier2:828-835): forecastValue = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d', aliasedForecastFirstDealValueSql('d')) [forecast_revenue-first chain]; weightedValue = forecastValue * CASE psc.slug 'opportunity'->0.10; estimating/under_review->0.25; estimate_sent_to_client->0.50; contract/contract_signed->0.75; ELSE COALESCE(d.win_probability,10)/100 END. The at-risk/upcoming list (:880-894) is the closest to a literal 'closing in N days' list: WHERE psc.slug NOT IN terminal AND d.expected_close_date BETWEEN dateFrom AND dateTo. A 30/60/90 view would bucket expected_close_date into now()+30/60/90 windows with one of these value formulas.
- DATE COL: deals.expected_close_date (date, deals.ts:169). monthly forecast trend secondarily COALESCE(expected_close_date, actual_close_date, contract_signed_date, updated_at::date) at performance-tier2:871-872. Forecast-variance uses deal_forecast_milestones.expected_close_date snapshot (reports/service.ts:404, 445, 490).
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: Feasible per-department on expected_close_date: join users/offices, group, bucket expected_close_date into +30/+60/+90 (or a Sun-Sat WTD 'expected to close this week'). MUST pick ONE value+weight convention -- win_probability/100 (default 50) vs the fixed stage-ladder (10/25/50/75) -- because they yield materially different totals. Note expected_close_date is frequently NULL (the win-prob report requires IS NOT NULL and silently drops nulls; the at-risk list orders NULLS LAST), so coverage is partial.
- PER-REP: PARTIAL/feasible but no single source. getWeightedPipelineForecast accepts repId and reps are auto-scoped to their own id at the route (GET /api/reports/weighted-forecast, routes.ts:204-217), so a per-rep win-prob-weighted projection on expected_close_date already exists and is what a rep can see. getForecastAccuracyReport is director-only (requireDirector, routes.ts:509) and uses a DIFFERENT stage-weight formula -- so a per-rep report built off it would not match what directors see vs reps. There is no expected_close_date column on the rep dashboard cards at all (dashboard has no 30/60/90 surface).
  - DIVERGES @ Weighted forecast (getWeightedPipelineForecast) vs stage-weighted forecast (getForecastAccuracyReport) (reports/service.ts:683-686 vs performance-tier2-service.ts:829-835): Same projection date (expected_close_date) but DIFFERENT weighting: win_probability/100 (default 50) and best-estimate value chain, vs fixed stage-percentage ladder (10/25/50/75, else win_probability default 10) and forecast_revenue-first value chain. Two different 'projected' dollars for the same deal.
  - DIVERGES @ Director Scorecard forecastCommit / forecastBestCase (getDirectorScorecard) (performance-tier2-service.ts:18-19 (COMMIT/BEST_CASE slug sets), :392-393): 'Projected' here is NOT date-driven at all -- it is SUM(open-deal value) FILTER by current stage slug (commit = contract/estimate_sent_to_client; best_case adds estimating/under_review). Ignores expected_close_date entirely; a current-state pipeline snapshot, not a 30/60/90 close projection.
  - DIVERGES @ Forecast variance / accuracy (getForecastVarianceOverview) (server/src/modules/reports/service.ts:387-478 (and :1809 getDdVsPipeline)): Projection inputs come from the deal_forecast_milestones table (initial/qualified/estimating/closed_won forecast_amount + snapshot expected_close_date), captured via forecast-milestones-service.ts. forecast_amount itself = deriveForecastAmount = awarded ?? bid ?? dd (forecast-milestones-service.ts:104-119), NOT the live deals.forecast_revenue column. Different value derivation AND a snapshot date vs the live deals.expected_close_date.
  - DIVERGES @ Schema forecast_* fields (forecast_window/forecast_category/forecast_confidence_percent/forecast_revenue/forecast_updated_at) on deals/leads (shared/src/schema/tenant/deals.ts:99-111 and leads.ts:104-116): These exist but are unused for the projection DATE or confidence weighting. Only forecast_revenue feeds the value chain (aliasedForecastFirstDealValueSql, deal-value-sql.ts:124-130). forecast_confidence_percent is NEVER used as the 30/60/90 weight -- win_probability or the hard-coded stage ladder is used instead. A report keying projection off forecast_confidence_percent/forecast_window would diverge from every existing surface.
  - DIVERGES @ Monthly forecast trend close-date COALESCE (getForecastAccuracyReport.monthly) (performance-tier2-service.ts:871-872): Buckets deals by COALESCE(d.expected_close_date, d.actual_close_date, d.contract_signed_date, d.updated_at::date) -- mixes projected and actual close dates in one axis, unlike the pure expected_close_date used elsewhere.

### SENT-PER-REP (amount sent to client per rep)
- CANONICAL: No dedicated 'amount sent' aggregate exists anywhere. The canonical 'sent to client' EVENT basis is entry into the estimate_sent_to_client stage, computed by dealEstimateSentAtSql() (deal-stage-history MAX entry into ESTIMATE_SENT_STAGE_SLUGS, else current-stage stage_entered_at). The platform's per-rep 'sent' surface is the deals list / kanban filtered by estimateSentFrom/estimateSentTo for the rep's own deals; the dollar shown per deal is the deal's best-estimate value (no SUM-of-sent metric is materialized).  @ Event date: server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:1018-1040 (dealEstimateSentAtSql) and workspace twin :1077-1099 (workspaceEstimateSentAtSql). Stage set ESTIMATE_SENT_STAGE_SLUGS at :401-404. Filters wired at :1062-1075 (list) and :1101-1114 (workspace); routes deals/routes.ts:577-583, 795-796, 876-877.
- COMPUTE: dealEstimateSentAtSql = COALESCE( (SELECT MAX(dsh.created_at) FROM deal_stage_history dsh JOIN pipeline_stage_config s ON s.id=dsh.to_stage_id WHERE dsh.deal_id=d.id AND s.slug IN ('estimate_sent_to_client','service_estimate_sent_to_client')), CASE WHEN current_stage.slug IN (...) THEN d.stage_entered_at ELSE NULL END ). Filter: estimateSentAt >= estimateSentFrom::date AND < estimateSentTo::date + 1 day. Per-deal value in the list = aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql (best-estimate chain: bid_board_total_sales>0, bid_estimate>0, dd_estimate>0, awarded_amount>0; 0 if on_hold). There is NO COALESCE(SUM(...)) 'sent amount' anywhere (verified: rg for SUM over sent / sent_value / amountSent returns nothing).
- DATE COL: Derived 'estimate sent at' = MAX(deal_stage_history.created_at) into estimate_sent_to_client slugs, fallback deals.stage_entered_at when currently in that stage. (deals.proposal_sent_at exists -- deals.ts:216 -- but is used only as a readiness flag in operations-tier3:539/497, never as the canonical sent date or a per-rep amount.)
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: Feasible per-department for a Sun-Sat WTD window using the estimate-sent event date: SUM(aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql('d')) WHERE dealEstimateSentAtSql() between weekStart and weekEnd, grouped by users.office. Caveat: the date is a correlated-subquery MAX over deal_stage_history (re-derived per row), so it is heavier than a plain column; and re-entry into the stage moves the MAX. Must reuse dealEstimateSentAtSql verbatim to match the platform filter, and reuse the best-estimate value chain to match the per-deal dollar reps see.
- PER-REP: YES for the SAME source a rep sees: scope getDeals/getDealsForPipeline by assigned_rep_id and apply estimateSentFrom/estimateSentTo; the rep already sees exactly this on their deals list/kanban. To produce an 'amount sent' number, a report must SUM aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql over deals whose dealEstimateSentAtSql falls in the window -- this aggregate does not yet exist, so it must be built to match the deal-value chain the rep sees, NOT awarded_amount and NOT forecast_revenue. Using bid_estimate-only or a different chain would diverge from the per-deal value the rep sees in the list.
  - DIVERGES @ Stage-weighted forecast treats 'estimate_sent_to_client' as a 0.50 weight bucket (getForecastAccuracyReport) and a COMMIT-stage member (getDirectorScorecard) (performance-tier2-service.ts:18 (COMMIT_STAGE_SLUGS includes estimate_sent_to_client), :832 (weight 0.50)): Here 'sent' is a CURRENT-stage membership snapshot (deals presently in estimate_sent_to_client), not a sent-EVENT in a date window. A deal sent last month but now in Contract is excluded; a deal sent and still sitting is included. Different population than the estimate-sent date filter.
  - DIVERGES @ Operations Tier-3 project readiness uses proposal_sent_at as the 'Estimate sent' signal (operations-tier3-service.ts:497-499, 539): Uses the deals.proposal_sent_at column (and proposal_status) as the sent indicator, a DIFFERENT date source than the deal_stage_history estimate_sent_to_client entry used by the deals workspace. The two can disagree (proposal workflow vs bid-board stage).
  - DIVERGES @ Two near-duplicate estimate-sent helpers (list vs workspace) reference pipeline_stage_config unqualified vs public-qualified (deals/service.ts:1018-1040 (dealEstimateSentAtSql) vs :1077-1099 (workspaceEstimateSentAtSql, uses public.pipeline_stage_config)): Same logic duplicated; a report must mirror whichever path corresponds to the surface it claims to match. Divergence risk if a report hand-rolls the subquery instead of reusing these.
  - DIVERGES @ AI-copilot SLA uses estimate_sent_to_client as an at-risk dwell bucket (server/src/modules/ai-copilot/service.ts:1120): Reads COALESCE(d.bid_board_stage_slug, psc.slug) IN ('estimate_sent_to_client','bid_sent','service_estimate_sent_to_client') for SLA dwell time -- current-stage membership, unrelated to a per-rep sent dollar amount.

### LEAD-STATUS (where a rep's active leads are in the pipeline)
- CANONICAL: leads table: l.status='open' AND l.is_active=true, with the lead's pipeline_stage_config.slug mapped to the three canonical lead-board buckets (new_lead, qualified_lead, sales_validation_stage). The authoritative active-leads-by-stage surface is the lead board (listLeadBoard / listLeadStagePage via buildLeadWorkspaceScope), GET /api/leads/board and /api/leads/stages/:stageId.  @ server/src/modules/leads/service.ts:1045-1089 (buildLeadWorkspaceScope), :1120-1174 (resolveCanonicalLeadBoardStageSlug + groupLeadBoardColumns), bucket slug sets :324-372. Status enum shared/src/types/enums.ts:80 (LEAD_STATUSES=['open','converted','disqualified']).
- COMPUTE: Board scope: l.is_active = true AND buildLeadOfficeScopeCondition('l',...) AND l.status = 'open' (default; overridable) [+ scope mine/team rep filter, + optional assignedRepId]. Each lead row's psc.slug is bucketed by resolveCanonicalLeadBoardStageSlug: new_lead = {contacted,lead_new,company_pre_qualified,scoping_in_progress,new_lead}; qualified_lead = {qualified_lead,pre_qual_value_assigned,director_go_no_go}; sales_validation_stage = {lead_go_no_go,qualified_for_opportunity,ready_for_opportunity,sales_validation_stage}. Count per column = number of open active leads whose stage maps to that bucket. 'Active' = is_active=true AND status='open' (not converted/disqualified); terminal/non-terminal also keyed via psc.is_terminal in some surfaces.
- DATE COL: None for status itself (it is current-state). Aging/stale keys off leads.stage_entered_at (board sort 'age_desc' service.ts:1095-1096; stale at-risk via getLeadStaleAtRiskResult on stage_entered_at, dashboard/service.ts:2845-2868). created_at is used only by reports' lead-conversion funnel windowing.
- WEEKLY ROLLUP: Status is a snapshot, not a period metric, so a WTD window does not naturally apply to 'active leads by stage' (it is point-in-time). Per-department point-in-time is feasible: join leads->users->offices, filter is_active AND status='open' AND psc.workflow_family='lead', group by office + canonical bucket. For a weekly NEW-leads or stage-entry rollup, key off leads.created_at (new) or leads.stage_entered_at (entered-stage-this-week); reports' lead funnel already windows on l.created_at (sales-tier1:169-170).
- PER-REP: YES, exact. buildLeadWorkspaceScope accepts assignedRepId and scope=mine (rep sees own open leads). The dashboard director rep-funnel (getDirectorRepFunnel) produces the same per-rep concept with l.status='open' AND l.is_active AND psc.workflow_family='lead' grouped by l.assigned_rep_id -- BUT with a different slug-to-bucket mapping (see divergence). For a faithful per-rep 'where are my active leads' report, reuse the lead-board buckets (service.ts:324-372), not the dashboard funnel buckets.

## 1. The canonical "this week" = Sunday→Saturday WTD definition

**Canonical source of truth:** `client/src/lib/pipeline-terminal-filters.ts:135-159`, function `toDatePresetRange`.

```
client/src/lib/pipeline-terminal-filters.ts:140-148
  if (preset === "wtd") {
    // Week-to-date, Sunday-anchored on the user's LOCAL calendar ...
    // getDay(): Sunday = 0. (Decision: WTD is the user's local week, not UTC -- see PR #539 ... .audit S5.5.)
    const start = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate());
    start.setDate(start.getDate() - start.getDay());   // walk back to most-recent Sunday
    return { from: formatLocalDateParam(start), to: today };
  }
```

Key properties:
- **Sunday-anchored**, `getDay()===0` ⇒ Sunday, subtracting it walks to the most-recent Sunday (`pipeline-terminal-filters.ts:146`).
- **Local calendar** (uses `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`, NOT UTC) — explicit product decision documented in the comment (`:141-144`). Note: this *reverses* the "F4 UTC-boundary" round shown in the commit message; the final landed body is local. MTD/QTD/YTD in the same function are also local (`:149-158`).
- It is **week-to-DATE**, not a full Sunday→Saturday box: `to = today`, not Saturday. The "Saturday" end only matters for a complete past week; for the live "this week" view it ends at today.

`"wtd"` is wired through the full preset machinery in the same file:
- Union type member: `pipeline-terminal-filters.ts:37` (`TerminalDateFilter.preset` includes `"wtd"`).
- Label "WTD": `:209`.
- URL since/until round-trip: `:232-242` (routes wtd/mtd/qtd/ytd through `toDatePresetRange`).
- localStorage parse allow-list: `:175`. URL param parse: `isTerminalPreset` `:306`.

**Consumers proving it is the ONE platform-wide week (D-7):**

| Consumer | Citation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Director rep-detail "WTD" quick filter | `client/src/pages/director/director-rep-detail.tsx:10,106-108` — imports and calls `toDatePresetRange("wtd")`; the bespoke `startOfWeekToDate` helper was deleted | Correctly consumes shared def |
| Deal-list page dashboard "week" period | `client/src/pages/deals/deal-list-page.tsx:147-153` — `getDashboardPeriodDateRange(period==="week")`, `diffToSunday = start.getDay()`, walks back to Sunday | Sunday-anchored, but **inlined copy** (does not import `toDatePresetRange`) |
| Deal-list estimate-sent preset (`wtd`) | `client/src/lib/pipeline-stage-page.ts:50-55` — `estimateSentPresetRange("wtd")`, `start.setDate(start.getDate() - start.getDay())` | Sunday-anchored, but **inlined copy** (third duplicate) |

So there are **4 places computing the Sunday anchor** (`toDatePresetRange`, `getDashboardPeriodDateRange`, `estimateSentPresetRange`, plus rep-detail which correctly delegates). Three agree numerically; only rep-detail actually imports the canonical. The two inlined copies (`deal-list-page.tsx:151`, `pipeline-stage-page.ts:54`) are a drift risk but are currently Sunday-correct.

**Gap relevant to reports:** `presetToDateRange` in `client/src/hooks/use-director-dashboard.ts:275-278` — the director-dashboard preset enum — is `"mtd" | "qtd" | "ytd" | "last_month" | "last_quarter" | "last_year" | "custom"`. **It has no `wtd` member.** The director dashboard cannot select a Sunday WTD window. So the WTD definition is consumed on the *deals/pipeline/rep-detail* surfaces but NOT on the director-dashboard surface the rebuilt reports likely sit on. Any rebuilt report that wants "this week" must import `toDatePresetRange("wtd")` from `pipeline-terminal-filters.ts`, NOT extend `presetToDateRange`.

## PART 1 — PROJECTIONS (expected close 30/60/90)

### 1.1 The forecast input fields on deals (schema)

`shared/src/schema/tenant/deals.ts:99-111` defines the dedicated forecast block, all **nullable / optional**:
- `forecastWindow` (`forecast_window`, enum) — deals.ts:99
- `forecastCategory` (`forecast_category`, enum) — deals.ts:100
- `forecastConfidencePercent` (`forecast_confidence_percent`, integer) — deals.ts:101
- `forecastRevenue` (`forecast_revenue`, numeric 14,2) — deals.ts:102
- `forecastGrossProfit` (`forecast_gross_profit`, numeric 14,2) — deals.ts:103
- `forecastBlockers` (`forecast_blockers`, text) — deals.ts:104
- `forecastUpdatedAt` / `forecastUpdatedBy` — deals.ts:110-111
- `expectedCloseDate` (`expected_close_date`, date) — deals.ts:169
- `winProbability` (`win_probability`, integer) — deals.ts:92
- Proposal dates: `proposalSentAt`/`proposalAcceptedAt`/`bidDueDate` — deals.ts:216-218

Enum values: `FORECAST_WINDOWS = ["30_days","60_days","90_days","beyond_90","uncommitted"]` (`shared/src/types/enums.ts:171-177`); `FORECAST_CATEGORIES = ["commit","best_case","pipeline"]` (enums.ts:180).

### 1.2 CRITICAL FINDING — the seven forecast fields are unwritable on deals

The deal update allowlist `applyUpdate`/`updateDeal` in `server/src/modules/deals/service.ts:1900-2103` explicitly enumerates each accepted field. It handles `winProbability` (service.ts:1950) and `expectedCloseDate` (service.ts:1951) — **but has NO branch for `forecastWindow`, `forecastCategory`, `forecastConfidencePercent`, `forecastRevenue`, `forecastGrossProfit`, `forecastBlockers`, `nextMilestoneAt`, `supportNeededType`, `budgetStatus`, or `decisionMakerName`.** A grep for `forecast` / `nextMilestone` / `supportNeeded` in the entire deals service returns **zero** matches.

The client *attempts* to write them anyway: the `ForecastEditor` (`client/src/components/shared/forecast-editor.tsx`) is rendered in `client/src/pages/pipeline/my-cleanup-deal-editor-dialog.tsx:57-68` and saves via `updateDeal(dealId, payload)` → `PATCH /deals/:id` (`client/src/hooks/use-deals.ts:576-577`). The PATCH route (`server/src/modules/deals/routes.ts:1820`) passes `body` straight to `updateDeal` (routes.ts:1968-1979), where the un-allowlisted forecast keys are **silently dropped**.

A repo-wide search (`grep -rn forecastWindow|forecastRevenue|… server/src`) finds **no `updates.forecast* = ` assignment anywhere** — not in the deals service, not in the leads service, not in conversion. The only non-test references are *reads* (reporting-service, sales-review/service, cleanup-queue-service, rfp-payload). **There is no code path that writes these columns from app traffic on deals OR leads.** Leads conversion (`server/src/modules/leads/conversion-service.ts:350`) carries only `expectedCloseDate` to the new deal — not any forecast field.

The forecast-editor UI also enforces nothing: revenue/gross-profit are free-text strings (forecast-editor.tsx:108-120, placeholder `"250000.00"`), confidence is an unbounded number input (lines 96-104), window defaults to `"uncommitted"` and category to `"pipeline"` when null (lines 67, 83).

### 1.3 What forecast inputs ARE reliably writable: `win_probability` + `expected_close_date`

Both are in the `applyUpdate` allowlist (service.ts:1950-1951) and exposed in the deal form: `client/src/components/deals/deal-form.tsx:471` (Win Probability field), validated 0-100 (deal-form.tsx:178-181) and submitted at deal-form.tsx:251-252. `winProbability` is range-validated again in the route (`server/src/modules/deals/routes.ts:1511-1514`).

Provenance / completeness:
- `expected_close_date` **is synced from HubSpot** — `scripts/refresh-from-hubspot.ts:330-331` writes `expected_close_date` from `crmDeal.expectedCloseDate`, and reconciles it. So it has real coverage where HubSpot had a close date.
- `win_probability` is **NOT synced from HubSpot** — grep for `win_probability`/`probability` in `refresh-from-hubspot.ts` returns nothing. It is only ever set by a rep manually in the deal form, or seeded in test data (`scripts/seedTestUsersAndData.ts:189`). In production it is therefore **sparse and unmaintained** — `getWeightedPipelineForecast` defaults it to **50** when null (see below).

### 1.4 What existing forecast reports consume, and how

**(a) Weighted pipeline forecast** — `server/src/modules/reports/service.ts:668-706`, route `GET /reports/weighted-forecast` (`server/src/modules/reports/routes.ts:204`, NOT director-gated; supports `repId`). This is the closest thing to a 30/60/90 projection:
```
TO_CHAR(d.expected_close_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
SUM(aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql("d") * COALESCE(d.win_probability, 50) / 100.0) AS weighted_value
WHERE d.is_active = true AND is_test_data=false AND nonTerminalDealStageSql()
  AND d.expected_close_date IS NOT NULL
  AND d.expected_close_date BETWEEN from AND to
GROUP BY month
```
- Buckets by **`expected_close_date` calendar month** — so a true 30/60/90 view is derivable, but only for deals that have a close date set.
- Weight = `COALESCE(win_probability, 50)` (service.ts:685). Because `win_probability` is unsynced/sparse, in practice most deals get a **flat 50% guess**, making the "weighted" number only marginally better than raw value.
- Deal value uses `aliasedEffectiveDealValueSql` → `bid_board_total_sales → bid_estimate → dd_estimate → awarded_amount`, zeroed if `on_hold` (`server/src/modules/shared/deal-value-sql.ts:108-110, 132-137`). It does **not** use `forecast_revenue`.

**(b) Forecast-accuracy** — `server/src/modules/reports/performance-tier2-service.ts:818-902`, route `GET /reports/forecast-accuracy` (routes.ts:509, director-only). Notably:
- "Commit" and "Best case" are derived from **stage slugs**, NOT the `forecast_category` field: `COMMIT_STAGE_SLUGS`/`BEST_CASE_STAGE_SLUGS` (performance-tier2-service.ts:18-19, 823-824).
- Its value head is `aliasedForecastFirstDealValueSql` = `forecast_revenue → bid_board_total_sales → bid_estimate → dd_estimate → awarded_amount` (deal-value-sql.ts:124-125, 27-30). Since `forecast_revenue` is **never written** (§1.2), the COALESCE always falls through to bid/dd estimates — the `forecast_revenue` "preference" is inert.
- Its `weightedValue` uses **hard-coded stage probabilities** (opportunity 0.10, estimating 0.25, estimate-sent 0.50, contract 0.75), only falling back to `win_probability/100` for unknown stages (performance-tier2-service.ts:829-835). So it deliberately ignores the per-deal forecast fields and uses stage as the probability proxy.
- Monthly bucketing uses `COALESCE(expected_close_date, actual_close_date, contract_signed_date, updated_at::date)` (performance-tier2-service.ts:871-872).

**(c) Forecast-variance** — `server/src/modules/reports/service.ts:395-433+`, route `GET /reports/forecast-variance` (routes.ts:343, director-only). Compares awarded amount vs forecast snapshots at `initial`/`qualified`/`estimating` milestones and close-date drift (`AVG(ABS(actual_close_date - expected_close_date))`, service.ts:431). **It depends entirely on the `deal_forecast_milestones` snapshot table.**

### 1.5 CRITICAL FINDING — the forecast-milestones capture pipeline is unwired (dead code)

`deal_forecast_milestones` is populated by `insertForecastMilestone` / `captureInitialForecastMilestone` / `captureStageDrivenForecastMilestone` in `server/src/modules/reports/forecast-milestones-service.ts:144,238,296`. **None of these are called by any production code:**
- `grep -rn captureInitialForecastMilestone|captureStageDrivenForecastMilestone server/src` → only the definitions in `forecast-milestones-service.ts`, **no callers** (not from stage-change.ts, not from conversion).
- `forecast-milestones-service.ts` is **never imported** anywhere in `server/src` (no `import` reference outside itself/tests).

So milestone snapshots are **never captured on stage change** in the running app. The only data in `deal_forecast_milestones` comes from the one-time backfill `migrations/0036_backfill_forecast_assigned_rep_history.sql`, which derives `initial` and `closed_won` rows from audit-log stage history (migration 0036:111-213). Consequently the **forecast-variance report has only stale, historical, backfilled rows and no ongoing data** — and its `qualified`/`estimating` comparisons (service.ts:429-430) will be largely empty.

### 1.6 PROJECTIONS assessment

What a reliable per-rep 30/60/90 projection *requires*: (a) an enforced expected-close-date on every active deal, (b) a maintained per-deal probability, (c) a per-deal projected value. What exists:

- `expected_close_date`: present (HubSpot-synced + editable), but **optional and unenforced** — `getWeightedPipelineForecast` filters out every deal with a NULL close date (service.ts:692), so coverage gaps silently shrink the projection. `expectedCloseDate` is only a *configurable* stage-gate field (`server/src/modules/deals/stage-gate.ts:74` is a label; gating is per-stage `requiredFields`, stage-gate.ts:299), not globally required.
- `win_probability`: writable but **not HubSpot-synced and rarely maintained**; defaults to a flat 50 — weak signal.
- `forecast_window/category/confidence/revenue/gross_profit/blockers`: schema exists and reports/sales-review reference them, but they are **write-dead on deals** (§1.2) — so any 30/60/90 view built on `forecast_window` (e.g. the sales-review forecast table, `server/src/modules/sales-review/service.ts:200-253`, which discards any row where `forecastWindow` is null at service.ts:203/227) will be **near-empty for deals**.

**Verdict: data is sparse and partially feasible.** A 30/60/90 projection can be built today only on `expected_close_date` (month-bucketed) × `bid/dd estimate` × an optional, mostly-default `win_probability` — i.e. essentially the existing `weighted-forecast` report. The richer, rep-curated forecast fields the schema was designed for cannot drive a reliable projection because **nothing writes them on deals**, and the milestone-based variance/accuracy machinery is **unwired**.
